description: The JSON envelopes the read doors wrap the protocol in. The contents are the protocol's own.

CallState.description: GET /v1/calls/{call}/state: the whole log folded, and the seq a stream resumes from.

last_seq.description: The seq the fold reached; a stream opens after it.

live.description: True while the log is still open.

LogPage.description: One page of a log: what this reader may see, whether the log is open, and where to resume.

entries.description: The entries this reader may see, in seq order.

live.description: True while the log is still open.

next.description: The last seq the page READ, or null when it read nothing.

SessionLine.description: One call as a list draws it: which call, how far the log got, and the state's own fields.

live.description: True while the call's log is still open.

channel.description: The door it came in by, once known.

from.description: The calling number or identity, once known.

to.description: The called number or identity, once known.

caller.description: Who was on the line, once known.

started_at.description: When media came up, unix seconds.

ended_at.description: When the call ended, unix seconds.

end_reason.description: Why it ended, once it did.

SessionList.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/sessions: which calls that agent handled, newest first.

calls.description: One line per call, newest first.

HeldAgent.description: One agent, as somebody choosing which to open needs to see it: its name and its channels.

slug.description: The agent's slug, which every other door takes.

channels.description: The doors it answers on, sorted.

AgentList.description: GET /v1/agents: every agent this fleet is holding right now, as the front page lists them.

agents.description: One row per agent, in the order their sockets claimed them.

KnowledgePush.description: PUT /v1/knowledge/{base}, the body: the tenant's folder as of now, sent whole. The base is replaced, never merged.

files.description: Every file of the base, path and text. A file not in the list is gone from the base.

GoldenQuestion.description: One question of a base's golden: what somebody asks, and the chunk that should answer it. A chunk answers when its file and heading path start with `expects`, so naming a file alone accepts any chunk of it and naming a heading accepts that section.

asks.description: The question, in the words a caller would use.

expects.description: The chunk that should win, as its heading path: 'tarifas.md › Tarifas › Revisión', or 'tarifas.md' for any chunk of the file.

KnowledgeGolden.description: POST /v1/knowledge/{base}/eval, the body: the questions a base is held to. A golden is fixed and the index is the variable; a question is never softened so a change can pass.

k.description: How many chunks a search may return, as the agent asks for them. Absent: the base's own default.

GoldenMiss.description: One question whose expected chunk was not among the k returned, and what came back instead.

expects.description: The chunk that should have won.

found.description: The heading paths that came back, best first.

KnowledgeScore.description: POST /v1/knowledge/{base}/eval, the answer: how the index did on its own golden. Both figures are computed by code, with no model, so two runs of the same golden over the same base answer the same numbers.

model.description: The embedder the base was pushed with; two scores are comparable only under one model.

k.description: How many chunks a search returned for each.

recall_at_k.description: The share of questions whose expected chunk was among the k returned, 0 to 1. The figure that matters: a chunk the model never sees cannot be used, whatever its rank.

ndcg_at_10.description: How high the expected chunk ranked, discounted logarithmically and normalised, 0 to 1. Two indexes that both find a passage are not equal if one puts it first and the other seventh.

took_ms.description: How long the whole golden took, in milliseconds.

misses.description: Every question the base missed, so the person who wrote the documents can read what came back instead.

KnowledgePushed.description: PUT /v1/knowledge/{base}, the answer: which base, how many chunks it became, and how long that took.

base.description: The base's name, as the path named it.

chunks.description: How many chunks the files were cut into and embedded.

took_ms.description: How long the push took, chunking and embedding included, in milliseconds.

KnowledgeBase.description: One knowledge base as the list draws it: its name, its size, and when it was last pushed.

model.description: The embedder that wrote its vectors. Two bases are only comparable, and a base is only searchable, under the model it was pushed with.

pushed_at.description: When it was last pushed, unix seconds.

KnowledgeList.description: GET /v1/knowledge: every base this org has pushed.

bases.description: One row per base, by name.

ContactFact.description: One fact of a contact's history: a MemoryFact with the two dates that bound it. A fact is never deleted, only superseded, so the history keeps every version.

id.description: The fact's id in the memory store.

text.description: The fact itself, as one sentence.

category.description: The tenant's own word for what kind of fact this is, from its memory.remember list.

source.description: The call this fact was extracted from, when known.

valid_from.description: When the fact was written, unix seconds.

invalidated_at.description: When a later call superseded or withdrew it, unix seconds; null while it is current.

ContactMemory.description: GET /v1/contacts/{contact}/memory: everything memory ever kept about one contact, current facts first.

facts.description: Every version of every fact, current first, then the superseded ones, newest first.

Forgotten.description: DELETE /v1/contacts/{contact}/memory, the answer: how many facts the right to be forgotten erased.

forgotten.description: How many facts were erased, every version counted.

MemoryQuestion.description: One question of a memory golden: what memory holds about the contact who asks it, the words they just said, and the fact or facts that should come back. The facts are the question's own, so a golden needs no contact in any table.

holds.description: Every fact memory holds about this question's contact, in the words a fact is written in. More facts than a turn asks for is what makes a question discriminate: with fewer, everything comes back and recall@k is 1.00 whatever the ranking did.

asks.description: What the caller just said, in their own words.

expects.description: The fact or facts that should come back. One answers when what came back CONTAINS it, folded for case and accents, so a golden names the substance and never the wording.

MemoryGolden.description: POST /v1/contacts/memory/eval, the body: the questions memory is held to. Each question brings its own facts, which are written to a scratch contact of this org, asked, and deleted. A golden is fixed and the ranking is the variable; a question is never softened so a change can pass.

k.description: How many facts a recall may return, as a turn asks for them. Absent: the runtime's own default.

MemoryMiss.description: One question memory did not answer whole: what it wanted and did not get, and what came back instead. GoldenMiss is the knowledge base's and names the one chunk that should have won; a memory question may expect several facts and miss some of them.

missing.description: Every fact the question expected and did not get back.

found.description: The facts that came back, best first.

MemoryScore.description: POST /v1/contacts/memory/eval, the answer: how memory ranked the facts its own golden asked for. Both figures are computed by code, with no model in the loop, so two runs of one golden answer the same numbers.

model.description: The embedder that wrote the vectors on both sides of the recall; two scores are comparable only under one model.

k.description: How many facts a recall returned for each.

recall_at_k.description: The share of the facts asked for that came back at all, 0 to 1. The figure that matters: a fact the model never sees cannot be used, whatever its rank.

ndcg_at_10.description: How high those facts ranked, discounted logarithmically and normalised, 0 to 1. A turn asks for six facts, so a question whose contact holds few of them is answered whole by any ranking and this is the figure that still moves.

took_ms.description: How long the whole golden took, the writes and the deletes included, in milliseconds.

misses.description: Every question memory did not answer whole, so the person who wrote the golden can read what came back instead.

ExtractionExpected.description: What must come of one call's hang-up: each field is one of the four ways a hang-up costs a business. Nothing here compares one sentence to another — a category is the class's own word, a value is a literal the caller said out loud, and a supersession is an id — because two ways of writing one fact are one fact.

writes.description: Every category named got at least one fact. The class's own memory.remember words.

never.description: No fact was written under any of these. The class's own memory.forget words.

never_says.description: The sharper half of never: no fact CARRIES one of these values, under whatever category. A card number the caller read out is what this exists for, and it matches on the folded words and on the bare digits alike.

invalidates.description: Every held fact named here was superseded, and — the mirror, which catches the model that supersedes whatever it touches — no other held fact was. A fact is named by its own text.

ExtractionGolden.description: One call written down and what memory must make of it: the write side of the table, judged by code. The read side is MemoryGolden and neither answers for the other — a call may extract the perfect fact and never see it again, because six is what a turn is handed and the seventh is cut.

name.description: What this case is called, in a report and in --grep. A file that names none is called after its own basename.

said.description: The call as it happened, one [who, what] per line: `caller` is the person and anything else is the agent. Both speakers, because nothing here is re-run — a golden about extraction is a conversation ALREADY held, handed to the hang-up's one model call.

holds.description: What memory already holds about this contact, in the words a fact is written in. They are shown to the model with ids, and an expect.invalidates names one of them by its own text.

plants.description: Sentences somebody tried to get into memory. Planting one IS the assertion: admission must refuse every one of them, whatever the model did with the conversation itself.

ExtractionCases.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/memory/extraction, the body: the goldens whole, as the tenant wrote them down. Each costs ONE model call — the very one a hang-up makes — run on the org's own model and keys against the class the caller is holding.

cases.description: The cases, in any order. They are run one at a time: a suite is run when somebody changed the prompt or the model, never on a caller's clock.

ExtractionBroke.description: One thing that did not hold about a case: which of the questions, and the evidence in a sentence a person can act on.

check.description: The field that did not hold: writes, never, never_says, invalidates or plants.

detail.description: What was found instead, naming the fact or the category, so the person who wrote the golden reads why.

ExtractionJudged.description: One case, run: what memory would have kept, what admission refused, and what did not hold.

held.description: Whether every check passed. False when broke carries anything.

wrote.description: What memory would have kept, one op per line: the verb, the category and the sentence.

refused.description: What the model asked for and admission dropped before the table. A planted sentence belongs here.

broke.description: Everything that did not hold. Empty when held is true.

ExtractionRun.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/memory/extraction, the answer: which model answered, how many cases held, and every one of them. A verb prints this and a pipeline exits on it.

agent.description: The slug the cases were judged against, whose declaration is the vocabulary they may name.

model.description: The model that made each extraction, as vendor/model. Two runs are comparable only under one model.

held.description: How many of them held. A verb exits 0 when this equals cases and 1 otherwise.

took_ms.description: How long the whole run took, every model call included, in milliseconds.

results.description: Every case, in the order it was run.

LookupRequest.description: POST /v1/calls/{call}/lookup, the body: which platform tool to run for this turn, and what to run it with. Worker-only; the gateway runs it against its own stores and writes memory.ops or docs.sources on the call's log itself.

input.description: The tool's arguments, whole and unread: the wire carries the object and never looks inside it, because what recall and search take is the runtime's shape and is documented in the runtime's own docs, not here.

speech_id.description: The turn's speech_id, so the entries the lookup writes join the turn's metrics.

LookupResult.description: POST /v1/calls/{call}/lookup, the answer: what the tool found, and how long finding it took. The output is JSON-encoded into a tool_result block, which is where everything from outside the conversation goes and the only place it goes.

output.description: What the tool answered, whole and unread: the wire carries the object and never looks inside it, because the shapes recall and search answer in are the runtime's and are documented in the runtime's own docs, not here.

took_ms.description: How long the lookup took, the search and the embedding included, in milliseconds. The worker's budget is 250.

Remembered.description: POST /v1/calls/{call}/remember, the answer: what the call taught about the contact, counted. Worker-only; the body is empty, the gateway reads the turns off its own log and writes memory.ops itself.

ops.description: How many memory operations the call produced: adds, updates and invalidations together.

took_ms.description: How long remembering took, the one model call included, in milliseconds.
